reaction_equations: CH3C5H4Pt(CH3)3 + Pt-Ox → Pt(s) + CO2(g) + H2O(g) + other byproducts
surface_mechanism_description: The oxidative decomposition of MeCpPtMe3 involves the adsorption of oxygen on the platinum surface during the air pulse, forming an adsorbed oxygen layer. During the subsequent MeCpPtMe3 pulse, the ligands react with the adsorbed oxygen layer, releasing CO2, H2O, and other byproducts. After complete oxidation, a new layer of adsorbed oxygen forms on the platinum surface, and this cycle is repeated during film growth.
evidence: The following reaction mechanism has been proposed for the oxidative decomposition of MeCpPtMe3 in the temperature range of 200-350 °C in the respective CVD process: Pt(s) + O2(g) → Pt-Ox. The adsorbed oxygen atoms participate in surface reactions at temperatures below 530 °C and a subsurface layer of nonreactive oxygen is formed only at temperatures higher than 530 °C. Oxygen desorption from a platinum surface starts at a temperature of 330 °C. Preliminary in situ studies with a quadrupole mass spectrometer (QMS) revealed that the reaction byproducts CO2 and H2O are released during both MeCpPtMe3 and oxygen pulses.
